text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Repair and maintenance facilities Singapore has made available to U.S. military will guarantee security in Southeast Asia, Indonesian Armed Forces Commander-in-chief General Feisal Tanjung says.
- Illegal betting syndicate raking in an estimated Singapore $2.4 million each month smashed by police on Saturday.
- China Finance Minister Liu Zhongli admits it would be difficult to achieve country's goal of a blanced budget by year 2000 as country's deficit remains stubbornly high.
- Fast-growing Sembawang Corp subsidiary Sembawang Kimtrans (S) considering going public in about two years.
- New Toyo International Holdings, regional manufacturer of specialised paper and packaging products, applies for listing on mainboard of Stock Exchange of Singapore.
- Gul Technologies will announce initial public offering today, and entire offer will consist of new shares.
- Plans by Mobil and Exxon to build two more petrochemical complexes here look set to go ahead, going by the latest burst of activity at the comapnies.
- China reveals sharp increases in revenue and unveils record debt issue and higher defence spending in 1997 budget.
- Thailand's largest finance company, Finance One, to merge with Thai Danu Bank.
- Chinese people's predilection for pork could threaten country's ability to feed rapidly expanding population, agriculture ministry officials say.
- Apollo Hotel starts recruiting more than 100 new staff ahead of completion of expansion plan early next year, general manager says.
